_VERIFIED: List id, statuses and custom field ids read live from the First Day workspace on 2026-09-10. Big Swing (f9135883) and Rock Reference (de6b3171) both confirmed present with their option sets.
_comment_backlog: 'Site Backlog' sits in the same folder as Current Sprint, which answers the spec's open question: sprint tickets DO originate in a separate backlog list, so include_timl must stay true or tickets whose home list is the backlog will be invisible.

taskQuery._TODO_subtasks: Alex to confirm whether the team uses subtasks on sprint tickets. Left false until confirmed, because turning it on inflates every per-person ticket count and would trip the unrelated-pile rule.

leadershipPriority._comment: Rock Reference. The quarterly outcome a ticket ladders up to.

customFields._BLOCKER: Task Owner still does not exist. Checked list, space and workspace level: there is no user-type custom field anywhere, so the ownership model falls back to assignees and the readout says so in one line.

bigSwing._comment: Created 2026-09-10. This is the field the cross layer rule is actually about: 'at least one, and really only one, big swing tied to a leadership priority'. Rock Reference says which quarterly outcome a ticket serves; Big Swing says which project it belongs to. They are different questions and the system reads both.

statusMap._VERIFIED: The Current Sprint list uses exactly: 'to do' (open), 'in-progress', 'vqa', 'qa', 'ready for deploy', 'complete' (closed). Note 'in-progress' is hyphenated, and vqa, qa and ready for deploy are all work in flight, not done. Matching is case-insensitive. An unmapped status falls through to notStarted and logs clickup.status_unmapped.
statusMap._TODO: Alex to confirm that 'ready for deploy' should count as in progress rather than done. It is the last state before shipping, so a ticket can sit there a long time and should still be visible as in-flight work.

_comment_bau: 'BAU' and 'Other' are real options on the Rock Reference dropdown. A ticket whose priority matches one of these counts as expected business-as-usual work: never a big swing, and never counted toward the unrelated-ticket pile.
_DROPDOWN_NOTE: ClickUp returns a dropdown value as EITHER the option uuid OR its orderindex. A real task in this list returns `value: 0`. The collector indexes both forms and always stores the uuid, since that is the only part that survives a rename or a reorder.
